tabInfo.callout_you_vs_market: Compare your metrics against industry averages and track your market share over time.

best-days-to-sell.dayOfWeek: These are your best and worst sales days. Launch promotions and increase ad budgets on peak days. On slow days, reduce ad spend or run special offers to boost sales.
best-days-to-sell.hourly: The darker cells show your busiest hours. Send flash sale notifications, social media posts, and marketing emails during these peak windows to reach customers when they're most active.
best-days-to-sell.seasonality: Use this to plan ahead. Stock up on inventory before high-demand months, and prepare marketing campaigns for Saudi events like Ramadan, National Day, and White Friday.

cart-recovery.funnel: Start with the step where the most carts are lost. Common fixes: show the shipping cost earlier, simplify checkout, or add more payment options.
cart-recovery.topProducts: Customers add these products to their cart but don't complete the purchase. Check if the price, shipping cost, or product description is discouraging them from buying.
cart-recovery.trend: If abandoned cart value is rising while the recovery rate is falling, set up automatic reminders by email or WhatsApp to win back those sales.

category-performance.table: Sort by growth to find the categories that are growing. A category with high revenue and falling growth may need new products or a promotion.

coupon-optimization.main: Coupons that bring in {{good}} SAR or more in sales for each 1 SAR of discount are worth keeping. If a coupon brings in less than {{low}} SAR, pause it or add a stricter condition, such as a higher minimum order.

customer-reactivation.overview: These customers used to buy from you but stopped. Send them a personal discount code or a WhatsApp message. Bringing back a past customer usually costs less than finding a new one.
customer-reactivation.topCustomers: These are your highest-spending inactive customers. A personal WhatsApp message or an offer just for them can bring them back.

demand-map.main: Cities labeled 'opportunity' have lots of demand in your industry but your store isn't reaching them yet. Run targeted ads for these cities and make sure you offer shipping there.

discount-rules.main: Rules that bring in {{good}} SAR or more in sales for each 1 SAR of discount are worth keeping. If a rule brings in less than {{low}} SAR, tighten its conditions, for example by raising the minimum cart value.

frequently-bought-together.main: Customers often buy these products together. You can use this to create bundle offers, add 'customers also bought' suggestions on product pages, or design 'complete the look' recommendations.

gender-distribution.main: Knowing who your customers are helps you sell to them. Use this data to choose ad images, write messages that suit them, and stock the products they want.

geographic-targeting.cities: If a city has lots of visits but few orders, something is blocking the purchase. Check if shipping is available and affordable there. Cities with high average order values are worth targeting with dedicated ads.
geographic-targeting.countries: Increase ad budget for regions with strong revenue and high completion rates. For regions with low completion, check if adding local payment methods or cheaper shipping would help.

industry-app-gaps.main: Start with the apps that the most stores like yours use.

inventory-turnover.table: Locations where stock sells few times a year hold idle stock. Consider moving some of it to busier locations or running a promotion there.
inventory-turnover.trend: If stock value rises while sales stay low, cash is held in unsold products. Promote slow sellers or order smaller quantities next time.

market-share.main: This shows your estimated share of online sales in your industry. If it's growing, you're gaining ground on competitors. If it's shrinking, competitors are growing faster than you.

market-trends.main: Compare your growth with your industry. If your industry grows 20% and your store grows 10%, your share of sales gets smaller even though your revenue is up.

marketing-channel-roi.campaigns: Your best campaigns show what kind of messaging and targeting actually works for your audience. Create more campaigns like your winners and stop spending on the ones that aren't performing.
marketing-channel-roi.performance: If a channel brings many visitors but few of them buy, review the pages they land on. If visitors from a channel often order but there are few of them, spend more on ads there.

order-fulfillment-speed.pipeline: Steps marked as slow take longer than the industry average. Speeding them up keeps customers happier and means fewer "where is my order?" messages.

orders-needing-action.main: These orders are stuck and need your attention. Handle the critical ones first to prevent cancellations. For delayed shipments, reach out to your shipping carrier directly.
orders-needing-action.trend: If this chart is trending upward, your operations aren't keeping up with order volume. You may need extra help in fulfillment or to automate parts of the process.

payment-gaps.main: Start with the methods that most stores in your industry offer.

product-performance.main: Products with high revenue deserve more stock and promotion. Products with few orders may need a better price, a promotion, or a replacement.

shipping-performance.main: This table compares delivery speed between your shipping carriers. If one carrier is consistently slower, try negotiating faster service levels or switch to a better option for that region.

slow-moving-stock.main: These products haven't sold well recently. Try running a clearance sale, creating bundle offers, or moving them to a more visible spot in your store. Freeing up this inventory makes room for better sellers.

stock-at-risk.main: Sort by monthly sales to see which products to restock first.

store-reputation.summary: Your Google rating affects whether customers choose you. Ask happy customers to leave a review, and reply to negative reviews quickly and politely.
